newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen - EMU delay possible if too few qualify.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen - EMU delay possible if too few qualify.

text.p: HAGEN, Germany, Nov 27 (Retuer) - German Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Wednesday that if not enough countries qualify for EMU in 1998, a delay in starting currency union should not be ruled out.

"A start date on January 1 1999 is not a question of war or peace; to threaten an end to currency union, or disastrous consequences for European integration, if there is a delay is a crass exaggeration, even irresponsible," said Jochimsen.
Speaking at a conference in Hagen, Jochimsen went on to say that the criteria for joining currency union should not be fulfilled using "accountancy tricks".
"It should not happen that the criteria for reaching EMU are reached by using some kind of accountancy tricks," Jochimsen said.

European nations hope to meld their currencies into a single currency from 1999, but have to meet certain economic targets to be eligible. Many are facing problems reaching these goals, triggering talk of a possible delay.
Jochimsen also called for sanctions to ensure that countries abide by the criteria for currency union.
"The stability pact being discussed at the moment and in coming weeks must be armed with sanctions to ensure that every detail of financial discipline, which EMU requires, is met," said Jochimsen.
He also said currency union itself was no guarantee of achieving European integration or of regularising standards of living across the 15 European Union countries.

He cited the difficult experiences of achieving German currency union after reunification in 1990 and pointed to Italy's Mezzogiorno (southern Italy) as a further example where currency union had not banished regional disparities in standards of living.
